text: Known as the 'mother of herbs' — carried by travellers for centuries as protection against harm on the road.
Hung by doors and windows against ill luck; burned to drive off unkind spirits.
Hung in doorways to drive away flies and pests; a symbol of strength.
Planted in churchyards against fearful visions and nightmares.
Waybread — thrives on trodden paths; laid on cuts to close them.
Sting turned outward: a ward that keeps small threats at bay.
Apprentice lore: lamb's cress only roots where water still runs pure — find the patch, find the clean source.
Pressed for juice into the Nine Herbs antidote salve.
Stirred with crab apple in the antidote; teaches the two-herb combine.
